files.reason: Documents presence-gated navigation, probe limits, caching and hardware-validation boundaries for the stated outcome.
Implements conditional visibility and worker lifecycle. Relative ordering and empty M1 behavior remain intact; saved-credential access and return focus regress.
Supplies enumeration, exact identity checks, serialization and attachment caching. Reviewed both foreground callers; reverse handle handoff and Windows attachment continuity remain problematic.
Adds the menu hotplug case without removing existing acceptance cases.
Integrates the discovery case and declares its scripted serial boundary; existing transport assertions remain.
Tests discovery, visibility, focus and cleanup. Its internal-PM3 open assertion can be swallowed before the attempted path is recorded.
Adds the fixture to harness-origin accounting. Reviewed the existing startup prelude's interaction with newly automatic discovery; actual device exposure needs wrapper context.
Adds visibility, selection, cancellation and single-worker checks, but does not cover returning from the selected decoder activity with the accessory still attached.
Updates disconnected-menu expectations while retaining stable-order, navigation and empty-M1 assertions.
Adjusts initial visibility expectations without removing lifecycle assertions.
Covers exact identity, bounded retries, aliases and menu-to-foreground cleanup. Reverse handoff and Windows replacement across pauses are missing.
Adapts serial doubles to the bounded readline argument without weakening PM3 result or readback assertions.
Records the new fixture in harness provenance. This supports testing rather than introducing a build-input or firmware upgrade.

required_device_checks: On physical iCopy-XS hardware using factory/no-flash and matching Iceman flash installations, check accessory-absent startup, accessory-present boot, hotplug, rapid replug and PC-mode transitions. Record actual nodes, aliases and USB descriptors; confirm no Who probe reaches the internal PM3 during enumeration or recovery. Missing equipment/evidence: an iCopy-XS and representative supported DIY accessories; original-accessory equipment is needed only if compatibility with it is claimed.

Exercise delayed identity replies, Read Credential cancellation, immediate return to the root menu and re-entry. Check handle release, responsive navigation, selection restoration and stable ordering. Confirm ordinary PM3 scanning before and afterward with one known supported tag. Exhaustive card writing and firmware flashing are not required for this discovery-only change.

For the documented Windows discovery behavior, test same-COM replacement and reconnect after retry exhaustion while a child activity is open. This requires a Windows host and serial devices; verify that attachment changes require fresh identity evidence.
review.summary: The 13 changed paths support one coherent presence-gated-menu outcome; no split is warranted. Rechecking the prior review confirms five introduced software/test issues and a separate pre-existing accessory credits violation. The prior smoke hardware-exposure finding is deferred to a coverage gap because the QEMU wrapper was not supplied. Firmware/Lua inputs, relative root-menu order and empty M1 behavior are unchanged. This is advisory, not merge or release approval.

findings.quote: self._menu_items = [item for item in self._menu_catalog if item[2] != 'iclass_se']
findings.trigger: A user has saved ICS credentials but the accessory is disconnected or has exhausted its discovery retries.
findings.impact: Hiding the entire activity removes the established root-menu route to saved-credential tasks, not just live reading. The unchanged ICSDecoderActivity exposes Saved Credentials, details, deletion and write preparation separately from _start_read. The supplied CardWalletActivity does not expose this credential store.
findings.requested_change: Preserve access to saved credentials through an appropriate navigation route while keeping live accessory reading presence-gated. Add disconnected-accessory tests for saved inspection, deletion and write preparation; no root-menu reorder control is needed.

findings.trigger: Launch ICS Decoder from the root menu, then return while the same verified accessory remains connected.
findings.impact: Every resume removes the selected decoder action before checking attachment continuity. Selection falls back to Settings or the next plugin action. When discovery restores ICS Decoder, selection preservation retains that replacement action, so an ordinary child round trip loses the user's focus without any disconnect.
findings.requested_change: Retain the intended selected action during pending revalidation and apply fallback only after confirmed absence, without overriding intervening user navigation. Add connected-accessory enter/return coverage, including plugin entries.

findings.trigger: While ICSDecoderActivity is open, reattach the accessory, start Read Credential, then back out to the root menu while the foreground identity handshake is still pending.
findings.impact: Returning the foreground handle releases _detection_lock before its ownership is resolved. The unchanged foreground caller at activity_main.py:9894 supplies no cancellation predicate and closes stale handles during later Tk delivery. A menu probe for the new attachment can therefore acquire the lock and reopen/reset the same port before the stale foreground handle closes. The added tests protect the opposite handoff, not this one.
findings.requested_change: Propagate foreground cancellation on Back/destroy and maintain explicit serial ownership through result delivery or stale-result cleanup. Keep ownership waits off Tk. Add a deterministic reverse-handoff test that holds foreground result delivery while the menu attempts to probe.

findings.trigger: On Windows, reconnect or replace a device on the same COM name while discovery is paused in a child activity.
findings.impact: Windows cache identity contains only the port path. If polling misses removal, a cached positive result accepts the replacement without a new Who/ISE exchange. A cached three-attempt failure also prevents retry after a missed reconnect. Hiding the entry on resume does not invalidate this cache.
findings.requested_change: Invalidate and revalidate entries when attachment continuity cannot be established, or track reliable attachment generations across pauses. Test both same-COM replacement and reconnect after retry exhaustion.

findings.quote: assert path != '/dev/ttyACM0', 'Accessory discovery touched the PM3'
findings.trigger: A regression in _is_pm3_port makes the QEMU acceptance case attempt a serial open for /dev/ttyACM0.
findings.impact: The constructor raises before appending the attempted path to opened. Production _open_serial catches Exception, including AssertionError, and treats the attempt as an unavailable port. The external accessory can then satisfy discovery, while the final assertion that ttyACM0 is absent from opened also passes. This acceptance case can therefore miss the isolation regression it claims to detect.
findings.requested_change: Record every attempted open before validation and retain boundary violations for assertion outside production exception handling. Add a negative control demonstrating that an attempted internal-PM3 open makes this case fail.

findings.trigger: Open the accessory activity's About submenu.
findings.impact: Pre-existing policy debt, not introduced by this patch: this submenu displays contributor handles rather than serving a concrete user task or diagnostic. Its static feature label/version does not justify a separate device-screen destination.
findings.requested_change: Remove the accessory-specific About option, _show_about, dead STATE_ABOUT routes and unused FEATURE_VERSION state in src/lib/activity_main.py, together with any tests demanding that submenu. Keep attribution in source/GitHub. Preserve the separate useful device AboutActivity and required legal notices; deleting only the handles is insufficient.

limitations: No tests, QEMU runs, CI checks or hardware operations were performed. The supplied test implementations and provenance-recording code are not execution results.

The prior smoke-boundary finding is not retained as a confirmed defect. guest_smoke.py:73 starts a menu that now schedules discovery, without an in-process serial guard in that prelude. However, tools/qemu_env.sh was not supplied, so actual device-namespace exposure is unresolved. Inspect that wrapper; an explicit empty inventory and fail-loud serial-open guard before the first menu would make the harness boundary independent of timing and host devices.

The complete literal search identifies tests/ui/activities/test_ics_decoder.py, but its full source was not supplied. Inspect its foreground detection/exit tests and any accessory-About expectations to complete coverage of the ownership correction and pre-existing submenu cleanup. Search hits alone were not treated as reviewed source.

The supplied startup and discovery sources reserve /dev/ttyACM0 and exclude resolving aliases. They do not establish physical enumeration across accessory-present boot or PM3 resets. This hardware uncertainty is separate from missing source context.

The new menu worker uses a queue and does not call Tk. Existing foreground accessory workers still call Tk.after directly, and target detection remains synchronous in the activity; those are unchanged debt, not introduced menu-worker behavior. This review does not certify the broader unchanged PM3, package-provenance or Lua-family contracts.

assessment.transport: All three submissions/poll sequences completed. No retry, truncation, timeout, unknown usage or validation error. INCOMPLETE is the final model coverage declaration, not a failed generation.
assessment.scope: Correctly treats all 13 paths as one coherent necessary accessory lifecycle change; no blanket rejection of core/startup modifications. Distinguishes source tests from physical proof.

findings.assessment: Source-supported UX consequence, but intentionally hiding the ICS entry follows the maintainer requirement. A separate saved-store route is a product decision, not permission to restore an always-visible decoder entry. Do not count this as an unconditional correctness defect.

findings.item: Focus loss on child round trip
findings.assessment: Confirmed on historical source and current main: onResume unconditionally removes the selected decoder row and permanently selects the replacement on rediscovery. Needs a focused lifecycle regression/fix.

Source-supported race: foreground detection does not receive cancellation; an accepted handle is delivered to Tk after the detection lock releases, allowing a resumed menu probe before stale-handle cleanup. Main retains this asymmetry; the separate menu-to-foreground closing fix does not cover it. No physical collision claimed.

Confirmed cache identity uses only COM path on Windows. Lower priority for the Linux device, but a valid documented-host boundary. Need explicit invalidation/attachment-generation design; not USB identity by VID alone.

Confirmed current test constructor raises before recording its attempted path and production _open_serial catches AssertionError as Exception. External assertions can miss the forbidden attempt. Add recorded violations and a negative control.
Correctly labeled pre-existing in the historical comparison; already removed on current main by #86. Do not refile it as a current introduced defect.

assessment.context: The final model explicitly requests tools/qemu_env.sh and tests/ui/activities/test_ics_decoder.py. They were absent from the fixed comparison snapshot; preserving that baseline was deliberate. The current CI worker uses bubblewrap --dev /dev, so no physical-device exposure claim follows from guest startup alone. Additional activity tests were inspected locally; no second paid run was sent to force a complete label.
assessment.evaluation_limit: One historical comparison, not independent human labeling or a reliability sample. Findings are assessed against source and user intent; none proves physical ICS behavior. Do not automatically apply model recommendations.
